svg.title: The three structural flaws of VPLS, and where VPWS, VPLS and EVPN each belong
svg.desc: Upper panel: three VPLS flaws. Flaw one, learning by flooding, because MAC addresses are learned from data with no control plane, so every unknown unicast or broadcast is flooded to every site. Flaw two, full mesh of pseudowires, so N sites need N times N minus one over two pseudowires and every new site touches every existing one. Flaw three, no standard active-active multihoming, so a dual-homed site blocks one link and wastes it, and failover depends on timers. Lower panel: three services placed by use. VPWS is a point-to-point virtual wire for one circuit. VPLS is a multipoint virtual switch for a layer-2 broadcast domain. EVPN is the same layer-2 service with a BGP control plane and a MAC and IP routing table, so it fixes all three flaws at once. A closing note says the choice is not about which is newer but about whether the customer needs multipoint and whether the provider needs active-active.
svg.text: VPLS is not a bad design; it is a design with three properties nobody wanted to pay for
All three come from one root cause: a layer-2 service with no control plane
Flaw 1 · Learning by flooding
MACs are learned from data. Unknown
unicast and broadcast go to every site.
Consequence: a broadcast storm at one
branch reaches all of them.
No mechanism to ask “where is this MAC”
Flaw 2 · Pseudowire full mesh
N sites need N(N−1)/2 pseudowires.
A new site is a change on every old site.
Consequence: 50 sites is already 1 225
signalled circuits to maintain.
The same quadratic bill as an iBGP full mesh
Flaw 3 · No active-active multihoming
A dual-homed site must block one link;
the standby carries nothing.
Consequence: half the purchased capacity
is idle, and failover waits for a timer.
No standard way to use both links at once
THE THREE SERVICES, PLACED BY USE
VPWS — virtual wire
One point-to-point circuit, carried intact.
Use for a single legacy link, a leased line
replacement, or a non-IP protocol.
Simplest to reason about: two ends, no learning.
VPLS — virtual switch
A multipoint layer-2 domain across sites.
Use when a customer needs one broadcast
domain and cannot be moved to layer 3.
Carries all three flaws above, by design.
EVPN — the same service, with a control plane
Multipoint layer 2, but MACs are advertised
by BGP instead of being flooded for, and
multihoming is active-active per flow.
Same customer requirement, none of the three flaws.
How to choose without an argument: does the customer need multipoint at layer 2? If not, VPWS is cheaper and simpler. If yes, is a dual-homed
site required, or will there be more than a handful of sites? Then EVPN, because VPLS will charge you twice for the same service.
Choose VPLS only when the platforms do not support EVPN and the site count is small enough that all three flaws stay theoretical.
